request: Automatically close new blank pop-up tabs after the extension blocks their destination.

baseline.observation: An owned popup remained open after its main-frame request matched a custom block and failed with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT. No blocked request reached the local server.

criteria: New tab with a native opener, first HTTP(S) main-frame navigation, within ten seconds.
Native rule-match event and blocked-request error must refer to the same tab, request ID and URL; the matched rule action must be block.
Recheck current tab, opener, pin state, pending URL and candidate identity after async reads before closing.
Successful responses, new navigations, expiry, tab removal and network-rule updates invalidate pending evidence.
preserved: Tabs that already received page content
notes: Native opener information also covers links intentionally opened in new tabs; a blocked initial navigation there is eligible.
The candidate map is local to the worker and is not restored after restart.
Cleanup requires native rule feedback: verified for unpacked Chrome and Edge; unsupported environments retain the tab.
The ten-second rule is an eligibility window, not a delayed-close timer. Network blocking still happens in the browser.
No browser API provides an atomic conditional tab close. Events and current tab state are checked immediately before the remove call.

review.fixtureModification: Cleanup runs add one inert loopback-only static canary to the disposable community ruleset; remaining rules are compared exactly. General blocker runs use unchanged source files.
review.generatedMetadata: Browser-generated _metadata indexes are excluded from source hash comparison.
review.unrelatedWork: Preserved; patch compares only this task against the pre-edit snapshot.

boundaries: Fresh disposable browser profiles; owned loopback fixtures; deny proxy; no suspicious domain contacted.
No packages installed and no personal browser profile modified. Reload the unpacked extension to apply the change.
Firefox tab cleanup is not supported by this feedback path; no Firefox runtime claim is made.
No rule compilation was needed because shipped list data and permission declarations were not changed.
